Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and for sending the attachments. A few clarifications from our security/privacy review: 

1) When you say "not used to improve models," we need explicit language that Acme data (including prompts, user messages, and message metadata) will not be used for model training, tuning, or evaluation unless we opt-in in writing.

2) Retention: we need an explicit maximum retention window for raw request/response logs (we typically require <= 30 days). If you have tiered policies depending on route (embedding vs chat), please call that out.

3) Logging controls: ability to disable logging at the route or API key level is important for certain PII-bearing endpoints.

4) Data residency: we will require US-only processing for the pilot.

Can you confirm these points and share the SOC2 PDF? Also, do you have a one-paragraph opt-out statement we can put in our procurement system / SOW?

Appreciate it — Tom and I will review once we have the language.

—Vivian
VP, InfoSec
Acme Corp

Thanks — good questions. Confirmations below and a suggested opt-out paragraph (draft) you can use in the SOW: 

Controls & confirmations:
- Training opt-out: Redwood confirms that, for Acme Corp, data processed under deal ACME-2027-09 will not be used to train, tune, or evaluate Redwood models or shared with model training pipelines unless Acme provides explicit written consent. This includes user prompts, messages, attachments, and associated metadata.
- Retention: default request/response logs are retained for 30 days. We offer configurable retention per-route; for the pilot we will set TTL=30 days for all routes.
- Logging controls: we support per-route and per-API-key logging toggles; we will work with your engineers to disable logging on any endpoints you mark as PII-sensitive.
- Data residency: we confirm US-only processing for the pilot environment and will route all production traffic for Acme to US regions only.

Suggested opt-out statement (one paragraph):
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer Data (including prompts, messages, attachments, and metadata) to train, tune, or evaluate models or for model improvement activities unless Customer provides prior written consent. Redwood will retain request/response logs for a maximum of 30 days by default and offers per-route and per-key logging controls to meet Customer PII requirements. For the pilot, all processing will occur in US regions only."

Attachments: SOC2-Type2-2026.pdf (attestation) and data-retention-policy-acme-v1.docx (policy draft).

Next steps: I’ve looped in Rishi (legal) and Neha (security) to help convert this language into SOW/addendum text. If that works for you, Rishi can propose the specific SOW clause and we can get signatures.
